newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Police arrest bomb man at B'desh Speaker's party.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest bomb man at B'desh Speaker's party.

text.p: Bangladesh police said on Sunday they had arrested a young man carrying a powerful bomb in a black bag during a reception for the speaker of parliament, Humayun Rasheed Choudhury, police said.

They told reporters that Arif Hossain Oli, who identified himself as a student activist for the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), was challenged as he "suspiciously closed in" on Choudhury at the reception, on the outskirts of the northeastern town of Sylhet.

"We found a powerful bomb and a toy pistol in Oli's bag. He is suspected of planning an attack on the Speaker," one police officer told reporters in Sylhet, Choudhury's ancestral home. "We have already started a police case against him while interrogation is continuing."
Police declined to give further details.
Choudhury said last month that he had received telephoned death threats from anonymous callers.
He told the Bengali newspaper Banglabazar Patrika on August 27 that such threats were possibly coming from "those who want to push the country into chaos...".
Choudhury was appointed speaker of the 330-member parliament on July 13. one month after general elections in which the Awami League led by Sheikh Hasina regained power after 21 years.
A former foreign minister and veteran diplomat, Choudhury also served as president of the 41st session of the U.N. General Assembly in 1986-87.

The BNP has criticised Choudhury for being "too biased" towards the Awami League, the party to which he belongs, and has alleged he is denying the opposition due facilities in parliament.It has demanded his resignation.
